analyst_view.overall: Werder Bremen (6th, 18 points) host bottom side Gladbach (4 points from 10) on Friday night. Daniel Thioune's Werder come off a 4-0 Nordderby win over Hamburg with Njinmah scoring twice, but their injury list is long: Mitchell Weiser and Marco Grüll missed the derby, and FotMob also lists Alvero, Musah, N'Diaye, Agu, Topp and Jens Stage out (Stage is not confirmed by a second source). Gladbach, under Alexander Blessin since October, lost 0-1 to Dortmund and are without captain Tim Kleindienst (out since September, back in December per Blessin), Leopold, Ullrich, Bolin and Leszczynski, with Honorat doubtful; most of these have been out for weeks, so recent form already reflects them. The numbers carry no player list for this game but already add Werder's strong recent shooting and Gladbach's rise in bookings; no referee is named yet. Nothing clear points away from the numbers, so I stay with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, 1.9 for Werder. Werder have scored 13 in six and Gladbach rely on Machino with Kleindienst still out, but both sides' absences are mostly long-standing and already in their form, which the numbers count. I stay at about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners. Werder's wing-backs Weiser and Agu are listed out, which could take a little width away, but they have been missing in recent games too and Werder still won corners against Hamburg. I stay at about 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards. Gladbach have picked up 20 cards in their last six, a sign of a struggling side under pressure, and the numbers already add about 8% for it; no referee has been named yet. I stay at about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.4 shots, 18.3 for Werder. Werder's 105 shots in six are already counted with an 11% boost, and Gladbach under Blessin play a 3-4-2-1 that has kept games tight but not shut them down. I stay at about 31.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, 7.0 for Werder. Werder's sharp recent finishing is already counted, and Gladbach's attack without Kleindienst has been thin for weeks, which their form shows. I stay at about 11.
